reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-4 fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: Which unit would you use to measure the length of a classroom: centimeters or meters?
Which unit would you use to measure the length of a crayon: centimeters or meters?
Which unit would you use to measure the length of a basketball court: centimeters or meters?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample asks the student to pick between cm and m for a real object (crayon, spoon, classroom, hallway), directly matching 'identify and use the appropriate unit to measure the length of an object', with sensible unit answers (small items get cm, large spaces get m).

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: None of the 7 seeds (42-48) present the 'distance between two locations' half of this competency (e.g. distance from home to school); every sample is an object-length judgment, so that explicit clause of the competency text is untested in this sample set.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The fixed sentence frame 'Which unit would you use to measure the length of [object]: centimeters or meters?' is a short, repeated, easy-to-parse structure suitable for grade-2 quarter-2 readers.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Object choices (classroom, crayon, spoon, shoe, basketball court, hallway) plausibly cover both the cm-appropriate small-object case and the m-appropriate large-space case, giving the two-way discrimination the competency needs even if the distance-between-locations case is missing.

competency_alignment.rationale: The content is squarely about choosing between m and cm for real-world lengths, matching the unit-appropriateness focus of this lc rather than drifting into estimation or computation.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Object choices span from a crayon to a basketball court, giving a genuine small-vs-large contrast that makes the unit choice meaningful rather than trivial for a grade-2 student.
